notes: OWN QUESTION (D006) fully answered from the full text. Volume: the methods state the volume injected per intradermal wheal explicitly (recorded in the paper card and in the D006 claim update's reason under the brief's exception; written as [dose figure omitted] everywhere else). Endpoint: complete recovery, not half recovery - pinprick analgesia tested every 10 minutes 'until full recovery occurred', duration timed 'from the time of injection to the last reported analgesia at the site'. DESIGN SETTLED: double-blind, within-subject/paired (all 20 volunteers received all three solutions as separate volar-forearm wheals raised with a tuberculin syringe), paired Student's t test, n=20, healthy young volunteers, University of Kansas, Human Subjects Committee approval and informed consent. NOT RANDOMISED: the words random, randomised, randomized, allocation, sequence and crossover appear nowhere in the paper, and no allocation or site-order method is described; 'double-blind' is asserted without saying who was blinded or how. COMPARISON AND RESULT: bupivacaine alone 139 +/- 78 min, the mixture 36 +/- 16 min, chloroprocaine alone 24 +/- 11 min (mean +/- 1 SD). Mixture vs bupivacaine alone p < 0.001; mixture vs chloroprocaine alone ALSO significant at p < 0.01 - so the amide's contribution was greatly reduced but not statistically abolished, which two Notion pages get wrong. VERDICT CHANGES: C033 narrowed -> refuted (the paper's own reference list contains two pre-1979 human studies of the same chloroprocaine-plus-bupivacaine mixture with block duration as an outcome: Cunningham 1974 PMID 4429221 and Raj 1977 PMID 556897). D006 narrowed -> narrowed, uncertainty resolved. C041, C045, D008 unchanged; D008 stays uncertain because the one remaining question the record flagged for it (whether any Reynolds-group study timed complete recovery at the smaller wheal volume) is not addressed by this paper.
